title: I believe 'triple A' game studios are going to dissolve and eventually vanish, and indie devs and smaller studios will dominate the industry.
author: Beginning-Chapter-26
selftext:
I've been seeing a pattern where indies develop absolutely beautiful games, full of love and care, like Pseudoregalia, Bright Memory, Stray, etc; and bigger studios creating buggy messes they'll 'fix later' like Cyberpunk, Gollum, etc. I believe, for bigger studios, there are simply 'too many cooks' or so many people that communication and organization becomes too hard to manage and the overall vision of the project isn't clear. I also believe the higher ups of many studios tend to 'overhype' a project and showcase something their team cannot create; to elaborate, look at Anthem or Destiny - a 'big trailer' or 'teaser' is released, showcasing so much stuff you could do in said games, the higher ups never bothered communicating with the dev team and the dev team panics, because, they know, the features showcased are not feasible at all. My heart goes out to devs that work for big studios, putting their own heart and soul into something, only for the final product to be released as a complete mess because of deadlines and poor management. Again, 'too many cooks.'

Then we have indies. Sure, many indies may wish to scam people and release pure garbage, but there are also many indies that have a love for games and wish to create something others could enjoy; something new and/or unique. They tend to have a low budget, not a lot of resources, and yet, they still manage to create amazing things. Many indie studios have just the right amount of people, or at least a very clear vision with very passionate developers.

All of this said, I believe 'triple A' studios (+100) will soon be a thing of the past, and instead we'll have many smaller or even single developers. I believe this will be the inevitable reality because of the advancement in LLM's and AI in general. Yes I am very optimistic about AI and machine learning. I believe AI will give indies the resources they need to create even bigger games that could rival games big studios create. Game engines, compilers, digital art software, etc, has made gamedev much easier. Once AI could do chunks of gamedev, like art, code, etc, indies could spend more time on specific things they love or broaden their scope. Unreal already uses AI for metahumans, and Epic, from what Tim Sweeney has said, does not want to be the company that halts innovation. Unity's CEO has made statements saying AI is indeed the future and I fully agree. I believe smaller teams will rise with AI, and because of AI, bigger studios will either shrink or disappear.

I cannot emphasize enough how big studios are just... too big and they tend to have bad managers; I'm willing to even bet upper management doesn't enjoy or even play games and simply desire to make as much money as possible with as little effort as possible. It's a business so I can't even blame them sometimes.
Lastly, which confirms my suspicions, bigger studios are beginning to close when the games they spend years on do not make a *ton* of money. When you have so many people, it's not only harder to just manage but also just too expensive in general really. Here's a link for more context and better explains what I mean by *expensive* : https://youtu.be/ObCDvnTYlLQ?si=mXlNgkHJJD40FIXY


What do you think?
